title: Yisroel and Yaakov: the middle line of truth, and the thigh that can be struck
overview: Before the unions of Yisroel with Leah and of Yaakov with Rachel, the chapter sets out the difference between Yisroel and Yaakov. Yisroel is *sar Kel*: the *Keser*, the divine will, masters the *chachma*, and Rabbi Markel stops to say that this will is total *bittul*, not "do what you want". Yaakov is *tiferes*, the middle line, the *vav* of truth. The right and left lines limit each other and their light of the mind fades as they go down, until *netzach* and *hod*, the thighs, are cut off: there the angel of Esav touched Yaakov, and the outside takes hold. The middle line is one from head to end: the *yesod* acts from the *daas*, mercy is as great as the knowing of the other, and the wish to give comes out of the mercy. So it is *emes*, the same at the beginning, middle and end, like a man who stays true or John Wayne's true grit, and "Yaakov did not die." In class the outer Yaakov becomes the observant Jew who works on his *middos* without the mind and limps; Yisroel, led by the head, does not lie. What is missing is the *hisbonenus*.

sections.title: Yisroel is sar Kel: the Keser is master over the chachma
sections.summary: The name Yisroel means *sar Kel*, master of *Kel*, which is the light of *chachma*: the *Keser*, the divine will, is the boss over the mind.

phrases.he: (לה) וזהו בחינת ישראל, שר אל,
phrases.en: *sar Kel* means the master of the *chachma*, the light of the *chachma*

phrases.he: דהיינו על ידי הארת הכתר בחכמה
שנקרא אל נהירו דחכמתא
phrases.en: the *chachma* is called *Kel*

phrases.he: שהכתר הוא המשתרר כו'
phrases.en: the *Keser* is the one that's the boss

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין כי שרית וכו':

blocks.text: *Chachma* is called *Kel*; Yisroel, *sar Kel*, is its master: the *Keser*, the inner *koach hamaskil* (power of insight) and higher, the divine *ratzon* (will).

blocks.title: "Do what thou wilt"
blocks.text: This is the big mistake of the Hermetic Kabbalah. They have a lot of nonsense, but the main mistake is their saying, "Do what thou wilt, that is the whole law." They take *ratzon* to mean what you want, and that, to do what you want, is *middos* of *Tohu* (the world of chaos). The real *ratzon* is total *bittul* (self-nullification), higher than *chachma*: not just nullification, it is not there at all. As was learned recently, from *chachma* on the soul has vessels in the body, but *chaya* and *yechida*, the delight and the will, are totally above the body. The inner will is not your will; it is the divine *ratzon*. They turn the whole thing upside down, into doing whatever you want.

sections.title: Yaakov is the middle line, and the middle line is truth
sections.summary: Before the unions of Yisroel with Leah and of Yaakov with Rachel, the difference between Yisroel and Yaakov: Yaakov is *tiferes*, the middle line, the letter *vav*. The right and left lines limit each other and stop; truth is what endures, like a river whose waters never fail.

phrases.he: והנה מעתה יש להבין ענין יחוד ישראל ולאה, שהוא יחוד המדות במחשבה שנקרא לאה, ויחוד יעקב ורחל, שהוא יחוד המדות בדבור
ותחלה יש להבין בהפרש שבין ישראל ליעקב

blocks.text: Next, the unions of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*: Yisroel with Leah, *middos* in thought; Yaakov with Rachel, *middos* in speech. First, what is Yaakov?

phrases.he: דהנה בחינת יעקב הוא בחינת תפארת דזעיר אנפין דאצילות וכו', שהוא מדת הרחמים כידוע שהאבות הן המרכבה אברהם בבחינת חסד דזעיר אנפין, יצחק בבחינת גבורה ויעקב בחינת תפארת וכתיב תתן אמת ליעקב,
חסד לאברהם כו' ואיתא בזהר על פסוק ונתתם לי אות אמת,
דא אות וי״ו,
phrases.en: that's the letter *vav*

phrases.he: בחינת יעקב שהוא קו האמצעי, בריח התיכון כו'

blocks.text: Yaakov too is *tiferes*, *rachamim*, the third of the *Avos* after *chesed* and *gevura*: "Give truth to Yaakov." The *Zohar*'s "sign of truth" is the *vav*, the *briach hatichon* (the middle bar).

phrases.he: והענין ידוע דקו הימין חח''ן, הרי קו השמאל בג''ה סותרו
כמו שמדת הדין סותר למדת החסד ומגביל אורו
ולהיפך החסד מגביל אור הדין
ונמצא שניהם נפסקים, שאין זה נקרא אמת, כי עיקר האמת הוא מה שיש לו קיום, כמו שפת אמת תכון כו' ועד ארגיעה כו' שהשקר הוא הכזב,
מלשון יכזבו מימיו,
phrases.en: a *nahar* whose waters lie

phrases.he: שהנהר נפסק כידוע
phrases.en: sometimes the water stops flowing in it; it doesn't always flow

phrases.he: ואמנם מדת האמת הוא המתקיים,
phrases.en: that means it's always good

phrases.he: להיותו כלול מב' הפכים דחסד וגבורה
באין מונע ומנגדו כלל,
phrases.en: so nobody is against him

phrases.he: על כן לא יכזבו מימיו כו'
phrases.en: that's why his waters never stop

phrases.he: וזהו אות אמת, דא וי''ו, קו האמצעי שכלול מחסד וגבורה, והוא דת''י
(כמו שכתוב למעלה באות הכ''א)
phrases.en: this is explained above

blocks.text: Right and left limit each other's light, so both are cut off: not truth. Truth endures, "The lip of truth shall be established forever"; a lie is *kazav*, like the *halacha*'s river whose waters "lie," sometimes stopping.
Truth includes both opposites, *chesed* and *gevura*, so nothing opposes it and it never stops: the *vav*, the middle line of *daas*, *tiferes* and *yesod* (chapter 21).

sections.title: The middle line is one from top to bottom; the side lines are cut off
sections.summary: The middle line does not change from its head to its end, because it is all one thing, connection. The right and left lines lose the light of the mind as they go down, so their end, *netzach* and *hod*, can be cut off altogether.

phrases.he: ועוד יש מעלה בקו האמצעי דת''י, שאין בו שינוי מראשו לסופו, כי כמו שהוא בראש כך הוא בסוף
ולא ישתנה מצד אריכות המשכתו למטה
והוא מצד חבור וקשר שיש בכולו, מראשו לסופו יחד כמהות א', כבריח התיכון המבריח מן הקצה העליון לקצה התחתון

blocks.text: The middle line also stays one *mahus* (essence) from head to end. *Chachma*, *chesed* and *netzach* are three different things, as are *bina*, *gevura* and *hod*; *daas*, *tiferes* and *yesod* are one thing, connection, on different levels.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ב' הקוין ימין ושמאל שאין בכל אחד מהם בחינת החיבור והקשר
phrases.en: they're not really connected

phrases.he: על כן לא ימצא בסופו כמו בראשו
phrases.en: the end is not the same thing as the beginning

phrases.he: כמו חח''ן, הרי בנצח יגרע אור השפע,
phrases.en: in *netzach* already the *or hashefa* of the *chachma* is not there

phrases.he: וכן בהוד

blocks.text: Right and left are not so connected, so their end is unlike their beginning: in *netzach* and *hod* *chachma*'s flow is already gone.

phrases.he: וכידוע בענין נצח והוד שנקרא תרין בדי ערבות
phrases.en: it's called the *aravos* in the *lulav*

phrases.he: שאין בהם טעם וריח
phrases.en: there's no longer the *taam* and *reiach* of the reason of the *sechel*

phrases.he: והוא מפני שנפסק בהן הארת המוחין,
כי החסד רק ענף החכמה, שהשכל והטעם שבחסד, כבר חלף ועבר עקרו
ולא נשאר בו רק בצמצום והעלם
אמנם עדיין יש בו בהעלם,
phrases.en: but still in the *chesed* the *sechel* is still there, hidden

phrases.he: אבל מופסק ממנו, ואין ביניהם חיבור וקשר כל כך

blocks.text: *Netzach* and *hod* are the *lulav*'s *aravos* (willows), without taste or smell: cut off from the *mochin*, the *sechel*'s reason is gone. Even in *chesed*, a branch of *chachma*, the *sechel* is only hidden.

phrases.he: כמו חסד דרועה ימינא,
כח היד ימין שנפסק מן המוח כו'
phrases.en: it's not connected directly to the brain

phrases.he: ובחינת הנצח שהוא ניצוח ההסכם לבד, כבר נפסק מן המוחין דחכמה יותר,
phrases.en: there's hardly any *mochin* at all left

phrases.he: כי לא נשאר בו רק רושם בעלמא
phrases.en: only a *reshimu* is left over from the brain altogether

phrases.he: מן האהבה וחסד
והוא כמו הירך הימין שנפסק מחסד שביד ימין כו',
ואין לירך חיבור עם היד כו'
phrases.en: it is not really directly connected with the hand

phrases.he: וכך ביד שמאל וירך שמאל, שהן בבחינת קו השמאל בג''ה, מופסקין זה מזה
על כן בסופו לא ימצא מראשו, מפני הפסק הארת המוחין, עד שיוכל להיות שם גרעון לגמרי,
phrases.en: in the final *hod* there can be a total *gera'on*

phrases.he: כמו ותקע כף ירך יעקב

blocks.text: *Chesed* is the right arm, cut off from the brain and connected only through a middle line, the spinal cord, the *chut hashidra* (the one thing a certain explanation got right): the matter of chapter 21.

*Netzach*, mere winning and agreement, keeps only a *reshimu* (impression) of the mind. The thigh is not connected with the hand, on the right or the left, so **in the final *hod* there can be a total *gera'on***, a total lack: the *chashmal* talked about later, where a person's final *hoda'a* (acknowledgement) can be *modeh* to something quite different from the original *sechel*.
This is what the Mitteler Rebbe said: a lot of what passes for Judaism is so close to *avoda zara* (idol worship) that it is really *mamash* (actually) *avoda zara*.

sensitivity.reason: Says much of what passes for Judaism is actually idol worship (in the Mitteler Rebbe's name).

blocks.title: "This is pagan worship"
blocks.text: What is *Yiddishkeit* (Judaism) and what is *avoda zara*? When the first tapes, the Inner Secrets, were just made in California, before the professional copies, someone was copying them by himself and sold one. The buyer came back: "This is *mamash avoda zara*. This is pagan worship." What he thought was *Yiddishkeit* was really Christianity. To him the matters of *Kabbala* are not Jewish at all; his Judaism was the whole anthropomorphic thing, with no *Kabbala* in it. Told that G-d controls the planets, he called it astrology, forbidden. Most of those ideas really come from Christianity.

sensitivity.reason: Says a Jew's idea of Judaism is really Christianity, and that most such ideas come from Christianity.
sensitivity.publishable: What is *Yiddishkeit* (Judaism) and what is *avoda zara*? When the first tapes, the Inner Secrets, were just made in California, before the professional copies, someone was copying them by himself and sold one. The buyer came back: "This is *mamash avoda zara*. This is pagan worship." To him the matters of *Kabbala* are not Jewish at all; his Judaism was the whole anthropomorphic thing, with no *Kabbala* in it. Told that G-d controls the planets, he called it astrology, forbidden.

blocks.text: So the final *hoda'a*: a person who just has *hoda'a*, like a regular *frum* (observant) man. In the olden days there were men like that. By our days there are men whose whole *hoda'a* is so disconnected from the *sechel* that it is not the same thing anymore; it has gone away.

sensitivity.reason: Says the observance of frum Jews today is disconnected from its reason.

blocks.text: *Hod* ends the *middos* proper, which run from *chesed* to *hod*; *yesod* and *Malchus* give to another. In *hod* the attribute is only a *hoda'a*, an acknowledgement of what it should be, and in the world, even among Jews, the *hoda'a* has it backwards.

blocks.text: Say we should go out and kill all the damn Arabs, and people answer, "Judaism is a religion of love." Not true: Judaism says that if you try to make peace with the enemy and it does not work, you go and kill them. By the *sechel*, with the *middos* of *Tikkun* (the world of repair), even an *ish chesed* (a man of kindness) meets an enemy who does him harm with a *sechel* of *gevura*, not of *chesed*.

Not true: Judaism says that if you try to make peace with the enemy and it does not work, you go to war against them. By the *sechel*, with the *middos* of *Tikkun* (the world of repair), even an *ish chesed* (a man of kindness) meets an enemy who does him harm with a *sechel* of *gevura*, not of *chesed*.

blocks.text: Yet the *hoda'a* insists on saving the butterflies; not that one should kill them, but it goes to ridiculous lengths, the *hoda'a* running by itself.

sections.title: Where the outside takes hold: the thigh, Yishmael and Esav
sections.summary: The angel of Esav touched the thigh, *netzach*, because there the light of the mind is cut off and the outside powers can take hold. *Chesed* and *gevura* themselves can be cut off too, less so: their waste became Yishmael and Esav.

phrases.he: שנגע בנצח, בגיד הנשה כו',
עד שמקבלים חיצונים משם
phrases.en: till the external powers can receive from there

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בזהר בענין ירך סוטה

blocks.text: He touched *netzach*, the *gid hanasheh*. Esav's angel, the Satan, can remove *netzach* and *hod*, cutting a person's deeds off from his inner *sechel*, till outside forces feed from them.
So the *sota*'s water reaches the thigh first: it is already disconnected.

phrases.he: והיינו הטעם גם כן בחסד וגבורה עצמן,
phrases.en: this is also the reason in the *chesed* and *gevura* itself

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אברהם יצא ממנו ישמעאל, שהוא מותרי ופסולת החסדים כו', ויצחק יצא ממנו עשו, מותרי ופסולת הגבורות כו'

blocks.text: Even *chesed* and *gevura*, love and fear themselves, can be disconnected, if less than *netzach* and *hod*: from Avraham came Yishmael, from the *pesoles* (waste) of the *chasadim*, and from Yitzchak Esav, from the waste of the *gevuros*.
We see a disconnected *chesed* in America: murderers let out because you have to be nice to them.

sensitivity.reason: A jab at American justice for releasing murderers.

blocks.text: They still have some light of the *sechel*, but not strong, so they too can be cut off, like Yishmael and Esav.

sections.title: In Yaakov's line, daas, mercy and giving are one: emes
sections.summary: The middle line is bound from head to end: the *yesod* acts from the *daas*, mercy is as great as the knowing of the other, and the wish to give comes straight out of the mercy. *Yesod* gathers all the lights, and so the line is called *emes*, the same at the beginning, middle and end.

phrases.he: אבל יעקב שהוא בחינת קו האמצעי דת''י,
הרי יש בקו זה חיבור וקשר מראשו לסופו,
phrases.en: this *kav* has a connection from the beginning to the end

phrases.he: עד שימצא בסופו כמו בראשו ממש
(כמו שידוע, דאין קישוי אלא לדעת שבראש,
phrases.en: a person cannot have a *kishui* without actually having a mental connection to the thing

phrases.he: הרי קשור בחינת היסוד בדעת שבמוח הראש,
phrases.en: the *yesod* is *mekushar b'daas*, with a mental connection

phrases.he: כאילו הן מהות אחת כו')

blocks.text: Yaakov, the middle line, is connected head to end, its end *mamash* like its head.
It reaches the *yesod*: there is no *kishui* unless he is thinking about her. The *yesod* is *mekushar b'daas*; without the mind it will not act, and it happens instantly, as one act.

phrases.he: שהרי הדעת הוא פנימיות, המאיר ומקושר ברחמים שבלב, והיו לאחדים תמיד
וכמו שאמר בזהר, משה מלגאו יעקב מלבר
phrases.en: Moshe, *daas*, is from the inside, and Yaakov, *rachamim*, is from the outside

phrases.he: והוא בחינת הדעת, שהוא פנימיות המדות של הרחמים
כי לפי ערך הדעת, ממש כך ערך הרחמים
וכל מי שאין בו דעת
phrases.en: everybody that doesn't have a mental connection to the other person

phrases.he: הוא אכזרי, כתינוק
phrases.en: he is *achzari* like a baby

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא, ויוסיף דעת יותר ירגיש הרחמנות
phrases.en: the more *daas* he has, the more *rachmanus* he has

blocks.text: *Daas* is the inside, one with the heart's *rachamim*: the compassion Jews feel is *mamash* one with the mind's connection to the other person. So the *Zohar*: "Moshe inside," *daas*; "Yaakov outside," *rachamim*.
*Daas* is feeling the other person, knowing him. G-d looked at the Jews in Egypt "and He knew," and right away had compassion. As much *daas*, exactly so much *rachamim*.

Without *daas* a person feels only himself, and **is *achzari* like a baby**: not cruel on purpose, but not feeling, so he hits another kid for fun. And **the more *daas* he has, the more *rachmanus* he has**.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות שאין בין הדעת והרחמים שום הפסק כלל,
phrases.en: between the mental connection and the mercy of the heart, the compassion, there is no *hefsek* at all

phrases.he: כמו בין החכמה וחסד הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like there is between *chachma* and *chesed*: it's two different things

phrases.he: ומכל שכן החיבור אל השפעת היסוד,
phrases.en: and certainly the *chibur* to the *hashpa'a* of the *yesod*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת התקשרות המשפיע אל המקבל
שהוא בא במהירות מן הדעת,
phrases.en: it comes immediately from the *daas*

phrases.he: כמו והאדם ידע כו'

blocks.text: So between the mind's connection and the heart's compassion there is no *hefsek* (break), as there is between *chachma* and *chesed*.

Still less is there a break before *yesod*'s giving: *daas* brings *rachamim*, and *rachamim* the wish to give. Real *rachamim* without wanting to help is impossible; the help comes straight from the *rachamim*, and it from the *daas*: *mamash* one thing.

The giver's bond to the receiver comes straight from *daas*: no real connection without knowing, judging mentally, what the receiver is. So "Adam knew Chava": the act was physical, so why "knew"? Of course he knew her; that is not the meaning.

phrases.he: (ויש בחינת נה"י בפנימיות
phrases.en: there's also *Nehi* in *pnimiyus*

phrases.he: והן כליות יועצות
ופנימיות יסוד סיומא דגופא
ונו"ה בחיצוניות הן תרין ירכין כו׳)
phrases.en: in *chitzoniyus* it's the thighs, the legs actually

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בזהר בראשית, בענין יקוו המים כו' אל מקום אחד, שהוא בחינת יסוד
שמתקבץ שם כל השפע,
phrases.en: all the *shefa* comes into the *yesod*

phrases.he: ונקרא כנישו דכל נהורין כו'
phrases.en: and it's called the collection of all the lights

phrases.he: והוא קו האמצעי שמבריח כו'
phrases.en: that's the end of the *kav ha'emtzai*, which is *mavriach* from the brain all the way down to the *yesod*

blocks.text: *Nehi* has an inside too, the *kelayos yoatzos* (counselling kidneys), connected to the brain, so they "counsel," *eitza* meaning brains. Outside, *netzach* and *hod* are the thighs, the legs.
"Let the waters gather to one place" is *yesod*, where all the *shefa* gathers, "the collection of all the lights": the middle line runs from the brain down to it, so it takes them all in.

phrases.he: ועל כן נקרא אמת, שהן אותיות
א' מ' ת' ראש תוך סוף של אותיות,
phrases.en: the beginning, the middle, and the end of the *osios*

phrases.he: שכתחילתו כן סופו,
שזה עיקר האמת
phrases.en: that's the main thing of the truth: it stays the same

blocks.text: So it is *emes* (truth), *alef*, *mem*, *tav*, the beginning, middle and end of the letters: it does not change. A true guy is the same with you at the end as at the beginning.

blocks.title: He stayed true to her
blocks.text: Of a husband they say he stayed true to her. Not that he is honest, or only that he did not cheat, which is lying: he stayed the same with her all the way through.

blocks.title: True Grit
blocks.text: Or *True Grit*, with John Wayne: grit is toughness, but why true? He is as tough in the middle of problems as in talk, not falling apart the minute something comes up; the same guy in peace, in war and after it: **that's the main thing of the truth: it stays the same**.

sections.title: Yaakov did not die; Yisroel is master over Elokim with the head
sections.summary: Death, the root of the *kelipos*, has no hold on the middle line, so "Yaakov did not die." Yisroel, "you have mastered *Elokim*", is master over the lower nature through *daas* and *chachma* in the head.

phrases.he: ולזה אמרו יעקב לא מת כו',
phrases.en: that's why they say Yaakov didn't die

phrases.he: מפני שאין אחיזה למות, שרש הקליפות, בקו האמצעי כלל,
phrases.en: in the middle line there's no death; it doesn't stop

phrases.he: מטעם זה

blocks.text: So "Yaakov did not die": death, root of the *kelipos*, has no hold on the middle line. *Daas* reaches *yesod*; *chachma* is gone by *netzach* and *hod*.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר כי שרית עם אלהי״ם,
phrases.en: you were master over *Elokim*

phrases.he: בחינת ב''ן כו'
phrases.en: over the *Malchus*, over the actual action in the world, meaning over the lower nature

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת הדעת והחכמה בראש
דישראל, לי ראש דוקא כנזכר לעיל,
ולכך אמר לו ישראל יהיה שמך
phrases.en: that's why he told him: from now on your name will be Yisroel

blocks.text: "You have striven with *Elokim*": **you were master over *Elokim***, *Malchus*, the lower nature. Yisroel masters it through *daas* and *chachma* in the head, "Yisroel, *li rosh*": his mind over his heart. So his name became Yisroel.

sections.title: The outer Yaakov limps; the netzach of Yisroel does not lie
sections.summary: Yaakov in his outer *middos*, *netzach* and *hod*, can be struck in the thigh and limp, and still be a Jew; Yisroel, the inner *middos* led by the mind, cannot. The root of Yaakov above, the Yaakov that did not die, is Yisroel; what the outer Yaakov lacks is the *mochin*, the *hisbonenus*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן יעקב מצד בחינת חיצוניות דנצח והוד, תרין ירכין כו'
phrases.en: Yaakov is only *chitzoniyus netzach* and *hod*, the two thighs: only the *chitzoniyus* of the actual thing that has to do with *maaseh*

phrases.he: שבאין מכחו של חסד וגבורה דאברהם ויצחק כו'
phrases.en: which comes from the power of the inner *middos*

phrases.he: על כן נגע בכף יריכו, בנצח דקו הימין, מטעם הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: Yaakov is the outer *netzach* and *hod*, the thighs, from Avraham's and Yitzchak's *chesed* and *gevura*. Outer *middos*, not necessarily by the *sechel*, can be cut off; so his thigh was struck.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 52-53 at w2106-2159 and talks about the outer Yaakov until he rereads line 52 at w2888, where the alignment marks it.

blocks.text: Is this a *goy*? It is Yaakov Avinu, who did not die: people working on what they think is *avodas hamiddos*, *avodas halev* (which it is not).
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 52-53 at w2106-2159 and talks about the outer Yaakov until he rereads line 52 at w2888, where the alignment marks it.

blocks.question: Then why does it say Yaakov Avinu did not die?
blocks.text: The text says "Yaakov did not die," not "Yaakov Avinu"; that Yaakov is really Yisroel. The point is that *middos* can go wrong. Real compassion stays good even as only a *midda*, but there is no real compassion without a brain.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 52-53 at w2106-2159 and talks about the outer Yaakov until he rereads line 52 at w2888, where the alignment marks it.

blocks.text: The *partzuf* (the full stature) of Yaakov is a regular Jew. Even an outer Jew who just keeps the *Shulchan Aruch* (the code of law) stays a Jew. His ideas may already be *mamash avoda zara*, as was said, but it makes no difference: he keeps *halacha*, he is a kosher Jew. He is a Yaakov, not a Yisroel, but not an Esav either; he is still alive. You can buy from his bakery, trust him, eat kosher food in his house. He is a *frummer Yid* (an observant Jew).
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 52-53 at w2106-2159 and talks about the outer Yaakov until he rereads line 52 at w2888, where the alignment marks it.

sensitivity.reason: Says the ideas of observant Jews may be actual idol worship.
sensitivity.publishable: The *partzuf* (the full stature) of Yaakov is a regular Jew. Even an outer Jew who just keeps the *Shulchan Aruch* (the code of law) stays a Jew. Whatever his ideas, it makes no difference: he keeps *halacha*, he is a kosher Jew. He is a Yaakov, not a Yisroel, but not an Esav either; he is still alive. You can buy from his bakery, trust him, eat kosher food in his house. He is a *frummer Yid* (an observant Jew).

blocks.text: But some *frum* Jews make their whole thing working on the *middos*: be a good Jew, be nice. Ask about *hisbonenus* (contemplation), and they call it *avoda zara* and say one may not study *Kabbala*. These are basically the *misnagdim* (the opponents of Chassidism): Yaakov means a *misnaged*. They fix up the *middos* directly, "as He is merciful, so be merciful," imitating G-d from the outside. The real imitation of G-d is the *nefesh hasichlis* (the intellectual soul) emulating the *nefesh haElokis* (the G-dly soul). Working directly on the *nefesh habehamis* (the animal soul), the thighs can become disconnected.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 52-53 at w2106-2159 and talks about the outer Yaakov until he rereads line 52 at w2888, where the alignment marks it.

sensitivity.reason: Names the misnagdim as the camp whose service is cut off from the mind.

blocks.text: They are *frum* Jews, and they are trying to be; they are not like the Reform and Conservative, who were really heretics and wanted to be heretics. We have gone so far down that *frum* Jews come up with ridiculous ideas and sell them as kosher Torah. Still, he is not trying to be a heretic; he is a Yaakov, and his Judaism is still alive: even a Yaakov does not die. But his ideas are not connected to *daas elyon* (higher knowledge); what he says is not *daas Torah* (the Torah's view) anymore.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 52-53 at w2106-2159 and talks about the outer Yaakov until he rereads line 52 at w2888, where the alignment marks it.

sensitivity.reason: Says *frum* Jews today come up with "ridiculous ideas" and sell them as kosher Torah.
sensitivity.publishable: They are *frum* Jews, and they are trying to be; they are not like the Reform and Conservative, who were really heretics and wanted to be heretics. We have gone so far down that *frum* Jews come up with ideas like these and present them as Torah. Still, he is not trying to be a heretic; he is a Yaakov, and his Judaism is still alive: even a Yaakov does not die. But his ideas are not connected to *daas elyon* (higher knowledge); what he says is not *daas Torah* (the Torah's view) anymore.

blocks.text: Yaakov is only the outside of *netzach* and *hod*, the deed, drawn from the inner *middos* of Avraham and Yitzchak that these Jews try to emulate.

So he touched his thigh, *netzach* of the right. The Satan can disconnect their *Nehi* from real *Yiddishkeit*: still Yaakov, since they keep Torah and mitzvos, but limping, *tzolea*, no longer walking straight in "the way of G-d."

It happened because the angel of Esav, the whole *goyishe* philosophy around them, the science and all that business, was able to dislocate their hip. But he is still Yaakov; he is just not going straight.

sensitivity.reason: Calls science and the surrounding non-Jewish philosophy the angel of Esav.
sensitivity.publishable: It happened because the angel of Esav, the philosophy of the world around them, was able to dislocate their hip. But he is still Yaakov; he is just not going straight.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בישראל
phrases.en: but in Yisroel this can't happen

phrases.he: נאמר וגם נצח ישראל לא ישקר כו'
phrases.en: even the *netzach* of Yisroel, even the total *chitzoniyus*: there'll be no lies over there

blocks.text: Not Yisroel: "the *netzach* of Yisroel will not lie," even its outermost.

The Rebbe says no way, and makes it *halacha*: seven-day creation against evolution touches Shabbos and more, and the Chumash keeps its plain meaning. In the Prophets the opposite: some prophecies are *meshalim* (analogies), not to be taken plainly.

phrases.he: כי ישראל הוא בבחינת הפנימית של המדות דחסד וגבורה בבחינת קו האמצעי דדעת כו' שנאמר בו כי שרית כו'

blocks.text: Yisroel holds the head, so masters everything.

phrases.he: וכן מה שכתוב יעקב לא מת,
phrases.en: where it says Yaakov didn't die

phrases.he: משום שנאמר ימותו ולא בחכמה כו'

blocks.text: The Yaakov who "did not die," as "they die, and not in *chachma*," is really Yisroel. Yet with *chachma*'s real *bittul* to the Torah, even the Yaakov who is not Yisroel follows the Torah, as the next line says.

phrases.he: (כן משאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה יעקב משמש במרום, שהוא בחכמה ובינה,
כי גדול דעה כו',
phrases.en: because *daas* is very big

phrases.he: והוא למעלה מהחזה כו' כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)
היינו מצד שרש יעקב למעלה מעלה
phrases.en: that's the *shoresh* of Yaakov

phrases.he: בבחינת הקו האמצעי דת''י, מטעם הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: "Yaakov serves on high," in *chachma* and *bina*, "for great is knowledge," above the chest: the higher Yaakov, his root, which did not die.

But the outer Yaakov that is disconnected is getting to the point that if this kept going a few more years, they would not be Jews anymore. They would figure out a way to marry a *shikse* (a non-Jewish woman), or maybe even a monkey; they could come up with creations. They are really disconnected already and it would become total, and that is why Moshiach has to come.

sensitivity.reason: "Marry a shikse, or maybe even a monkey," said of observant Jews.
sensitivity.publishable: But the outer Yaakov that is disconnected is getting to the point that if this kept going a few more years, they would not be Jews anymore. They are really disconnected already and it would become total, and that is why Moshiach has to come.

blocks.text: These are Jews whose whole matter started off not only to be religious themselves but to bring other people into the religion, and still the Satan was able to get them, because we are already on such a low level. It says Moshiach comes either in a very high generation or in a generation that is totally gone, and our generation is basically totally gone already. They are still *frum* people and already coming up with stuff like that; if not for Moshiach, very soon the whole thing would fall apart.

sensitivity.reason: Says a group of observant, outreach-minded Jews has been taken by the Satan, and the generation is totally gone.
sensitivity.publishable: Even Jews whose whole matter started off not only to be religious themselves but to bring other people into the religion can be caught, because we are already on such a low level. It says Moshiach comes either in a very high generation or in a generation that is totally gone, and our generation is basically totally gone already. If not for Moshiach, very soon the whole thing would fall apart.

phrases.he: אבל בחיצוניות המדות דיעקב נאמר ויגע בכף יריכו כו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר ודי למבין

blocks.text: The Yaakov that did not die is the inside. Of the outer *middos*, "he touched his thigh": there the Satan, once anything is disconnected, can cut them off totally, to death.

In fact most of the Reform, the Conservative and the *freie Yidden* (non-observant Jews) did not deny the religion. They came to America and became disconnected. Unlike the original Reformers, Herzl and all those people, who went against *frumkeit* (observance), many simply fell away, because they were Yaakov: they did not know that much, and slowly they got mixed in.

sensitivity.reason: Groups Herzl with "the original Reformers" who went against observance (Herzl led the Zionist movement, not Reform).

blocks.title: The grandfather, the lawyer and the cyberfreak
blocks.text: In many families the grandfather keeps Shabbos and kosher, the son is a lawyer, the grandson a cyberfreak at our *yeshiva*. The Cyber Yeshiva reverses this, back to Yisroel's *hisbonenus*: that is Moshiach's business.
What is missing is the *mochin*, the *hisbonenus*: the whole difference between Yisroel and Yaakov. End of chapter.

reviewQuestions.question: Why are the right and left lines "not truth", and what makes the middle line truth?
What do the willows of the lulav, the arm and the thigh show about *netzach* and *hod*?
How are *daas*, mercy and the wish to give one thing in the middle line, and why is a baby cruel?
What does "true" mean in "he stayed true to her" and in *True Grit*, and how does it explain the letters of *emes*?
Why could the angel of Esav touch Yaakov's thigh, and why can the *netzach* of Yisroel not lie?
Which Yaakov "did not die," and which can be struck?

notes.text: Class 202 (Sofer times) holds the end of chapter 34 before w1831; this file cites only w1831-3285. The side ends mid-sentence (w3283-3285, "It's like") and class 203 opens by finishing the thought on the final hoda'a (w0-358) before reading the last words of line 31 (w359-373); those blocks are under lines 27-31 with outOfPlace.
Line 1: the phrase English is cut from one sentence (202 w1848-1869), so the phrase on "sar Kel" cites words after the one on "chachma is called Kel".
"Do what thou wilt, that is the whole law" is the motto of Aleister Crowley's Thelema; Rabbi Markel ascribes it to the Hermetic Kabbalah. Left as he said it.
Line 2: he reads "כמו שמבואר במקום אחר בענין כיסא אריסא" on the reread (202 w2135-2150); the transcript has misheard "כי שרית".

Line 27 (202 w2703-2751): "chapter 21 is the next chapter we got to work on ... the one thing that he had in his explanations that was correct, that the chut hashidra is the middle line." Who "he" is, and what work on chapter 21 is meant (perhaps the translation), cannot be told from the tape; the block says only "a certain explanation".
The story of the first tapes (202 w2968-3200) involves a listener who copied and sold them; the block leaves him unnamed as "someone".
Line 36: he reads "כאילו הם מעשה אחד" for the printed "כאילו הן מהות אחת" and explains "one maaseh"; the block follows the line ("as if it were one thing") and the phrase has no English.
Line 39 (203 w919-980): "as it said just recently" that G-d looked at the Jews in Egypt "and He knew" (Shemos 2:25) is presumably the weekly portion.

Lines 52-53: he first reads them at 203 w2106-2159, then goes off into the outer Yaakov and the frum Jews (w2160-3111), rereading line 52 at w2888. The question block (w2227-2339) is a back-and-forth: the question "why does it say Yaakov Avinu did not die?" seems to be a listener's; the exchange is hard to follow, and the block keeps only his clear points.

Line 54 (203 w3143-3276): his words on the Prophets are tangled ("In Navi you can take it out of pshat ... Not only you can't take the pshat, you shouldn't take the pshat"); the block reads them as: in the Prophets some prophecies are meshalim, and sometimes one should not take the plain meaning. Check against the audio.
Line 55: he reads "בבחינת כוונה וצד הדעת, ולכשנקיטא רישא" for the printed text, and renders "then you're master of everything"; the phrase has no English.
Line 57: he first says "chesed and bina"; a listener asks, and he corrects himself to chachma and bina (203 w3422-3446). The text follows the correction.
Line 58: the reread at 203 w3760-3771 ("בחינת כוונה צדקתה דהיא מכאן ומעלה") is garbled; omitted as reading.
Line 59: he names Herzl among "the original Reformers"; Herzl led political Zionism, not the Reform movement. Flagged other.
Chashmal (202 w2861-2928, 203 w296-358) is "talked about later", in a later chapter.
